title: feat(components): declare `buttonVariant` in the toast and sonner registry inputs
body:
Fixes #7316

`buttonVariant` was real end to end and invisible anyway: declared on the TS type for both
`toast` and `sonner`, read by both renderers, and absent from both registry meta `inputs`
arrays. Both registrations now declare it. Nothing on the render path changes.

Angle-bracket-shaped tokens are spelled out in words throughout this body: GitHub's body
sanitizer deletes them, including inside backticks and fenced blocks (AGENTS.md, "GitHub
會改寫你寫進 issue/PR 正文的字節"). So "the Button element's `variant` prop", not the JSX
spelling.

## The three surfaces, re-derived by CONTENT at this branch point

The card measured `feedback.ts:175` / `:255` at `67dadd6`; triage re-derived `:179` / `:259`
at `a472b07`. Both are stale again. Located by content at `cf601fff6`, every address here is
a **third** reading and will drift too:

| surface | where | state |
|---|---|---|
| TS type | `packages/types/src/feedback.ts:336` (`ToastSchema`), `:641` (`SonnerSchema`) | declared |
| renderer | `packages/components/src/renderers/feedback/toast.tsx:30`, `sonner.tsx:36` | read |
| registry `inputs` | `toast.tsx:38`, `sonner.tsx:48` | **omitted** |

Each zero has its own lit control, as triage asked:

- tree-wide `git grep -c "name: 'buttonVariant'"` returned **exit 1 / no match**, while the
  same pass found `inputs: [` in both files and `name: 'buttonLabel'` in both — so the
  instrument was looking at the right registry shape.
- the six tokens were read off the TS union at both sites rather than copied from the card.
  The two lines are **byte-identical** (`md5 2f634a8c007eab9b8ac7ba3362d136f2` each):
  `default`, `secondary`, `destructive`, `outline`, `ghost`, `link`. The two spellings agree.

## Triage boundary 1 is falsified on its literal wording, and honoured on its intent

Triage said `type: 'select'`. **`'select'` is not a member of `ComponentInputControlType`**
(`packages/types/src/base.ts`), whose eleven literals are `string`, `number`, `boolean`,
`enum`, `array`, `object`, `color`, `date`, `code`, `file`, `slot`. Writing it would be a
`tsc` error here and a named parse refusal in the Zod twin. This repository's closed-list arm
is `type: 'enum'` plus an `enum` array — which is exactly what the sibling `variant` key on
these same two nodes has always used.

That is not a weaker substitute. `enum` is the **one arm `validateTree` judges exactly**, and
it answers at `error` severity, so it is strictly stronger than what boundary 2 asked for.

## Why this was not cosmetic, and what the new refusal costs

`inputs` is what the JSX-page compiler builds its prop whitelist from (`renderers/layout/page.tsx`,
`getJsxManifest`), and `sdui-parser`'s `validateTree` reports any prop absent from it as
`unknown-prop`. So an author writing `buttonVariant` on a page was **warned about a key the
renderer then honoured** — the same failure objectui#3808 named for `element:text_input.defaultValue`.
The designer property panel and the palette read the same array.

⚠️ **A new refusal, stated as such.** On the html/jsx page tier an `error`-severity diagnostic
fails the whole page render. So a `toast` or `sonner` node authoring a `buttonVariant` outside
the six now fails its page instead of rendering. That is the point of the closed list — `cva`
contributes no variant class for an unrecognised key, so `buttonVariant: 'primary'` used to
draw a button with no background and no text colour, and `buttonVariant: ''` used to resolve
silently to the default look. **Blast radius, measured not assumed:** every `buttonVariant`
value authored anywhere in this repository is `destructive` or `outline`, both inside the six;
the only other occurrences of an out-of-set value are prose in docblocks and changesets that
describe the trap.

## The parity family: run before and after, and it is silent either way

⭐ This is the interesting half, and it falsifies the card's own closing suggestion that the
existing gates would "take it from there".

| state | parity family | verdict on this key |
|---|---|---|
| branch point (both entries absent, files byte-identical to `cf601fff6`) | 9 files, **341 passed**, exit 0 | silent |
| toast entry removed only | 9 files, **341 passed**, exit 0 | silent |
| this branch | 9 files, **341 passed**, exit 0 | silent |

It is silent because `toast` and `sonner` are **outside its population**. The gate derives the
judged set from `@objectstack/spec` `ComponentPropsMap`; measured at the installed
`@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`, that map has 45 entries, neither `toast` nor `sonner` is one of
them, and no key matches `/toast|sonner/i` — against a lit control that `page:header` IS
present. `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` mentions neither node, against a lit control of
10 `record-picker` mentions in the same read.

⇒ **Declaring the input does not hand the key to that family.** Without a pin of its own the
key would be declared and still unjudged, which is the card's complaint one level up. Hence
`packages/components/src/__tests__/toast-sonner-button-variant-inputs-7316.test.ts`, which
reads the expected vocabulary off the two Zod mirrors rather than restating it, measures every
member against `buttonVariants` itself, and drives the real manifest validator.

## Ablation — the two registries are separate surfaces

Both legs mutate on disk, prove the mutation landed by grep count, and restore against `HEAD`
with a byte-hash comparison (`git diff HEAD` empty, blob hashes equal). No rebuild is involved
and none is needed: the root vitest alias table resolves `@object-ui/core`, `@object-ui/types`
and `@object-ui/sdui-parser` to `src`, and the pin imports the two renderers by relative path,
so nothing under test is served from `dist`.

| leg | pin test | parity family |
|---|---|---|
| remove the **toast** entry only | **10 failed / 8 passed** — every failure names `toast`, plus the one cross-node assertion. **Zero failures name `sonner`.** | 341 passed, exit 0 |
| remove **both** (= branch point) | **17 failed / 1 passed** — the survivor is the pure `buttonVariants` trap measurement, which does not read the registry | 341 passed, exit 0 |
| unmutated | 18 passed | 341 passed, exit 0 |

The first ablation also earned a real fix: three assertions passed **vacuously** on an empty
declared list (an empty list contains no trap, refuses no value, and equals the other empty
list). Each now asserts a non-empty vocabulary first — that is the second commit.

## Negative control on the trap

The declared `enum` cannot express either trap, and each trap is a trap for a **different**
measured reason:

- `buttonVariants({ variant: 'primary' })` equals the unrecognised-key output — no variant
  class at all.
- `buttonVariants({ variant: '' })` equals `buttonVariants({ variant: 'default' })` and is
  **not** the unrecognised-key output — falsy, so `cva` falls back to `defaultVariants`.

Driven through the real manifest validator, each node answers each trap with exactly one
`invalid-enum` diagnostic at `error` severity, stays silent on a declared value, and no longer
reports the key as `unknown-prop` — against a lit control that an undeclared probe key still
does.

## ⚠️ One diff widening, declared rather than quiet

Triage boundary 3 asked me to report anything the family surfaced instead of silencing it.
`scripts/__tests__/check-component-surface-parity.test.ts` cited this card's shape as the
**live** specimen for "an omission is legal". This branch settles that specimen, so the prose
would have shipped false. The fixture and the assertion are **unchanged** and deliberately
kept — the subset rule is not retired by one specimen being fixed — and only the comment says
so now. Fifth file in the diff; no assertion changed.

## Verification

At `1b352b2fb`, all foreground, exit codes captured before any pipe:

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/components build` — exit 0, 0 type errors.
  ⚠️ The first attempt reported **339** errors, all cold-closure (253 `TS2307` "cannot find
  module `@object-ui/…`" plus their `TS7006` consequences) — including on untouched
  `toaster.tsx`, the lit control. `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/components^...' build` first,
  then it is clean.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/components type-check` — exit 0. It is `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p
  tsconfig.test.json`, and `--listFiles` confirms the new test IS a program input of the
  second (the package's own `tsconfig.json` excludes `**/__tests__/**`).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/components lint` — exit 0, 0 errors, 953 pre-existing warnings.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/components/` — **277 files, 2717 tests, exit 0**.
- parity family + the new pin — 10 files, 359 tests, exit 0.
- `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:component-surface-parity`,
  `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:registry-bare-names`,
  `check:test-path-roots`, `check-changeset-presence` — all exit 0.
- `check:sdui-registration-pins` — **NOT MEASURED**, exit 2 `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`: it needs
  an `apps/console` build to weigh, and it says so itself rather than passing on nothing.
- Repo-wide `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` are CI's runs, not owed here.

## Not in scope, named so it is not read as settled

The opposite direction — dropping `buttonVariant` from the TS type and the renderers as a
non-authorable prop — is a behaviour change and needs its own ruling; it is not attempted or
suggested here. Refs objectui#4631 (three-surface meta-card), objectui#7268 (tooltip sibling),
objectui#6541 (mirror-vs-TS, a different surface, already settled). objectui#8941 touches
`renderers/action/` and `form/__tests__/`, disjoint from `renderers/feedback/`. None of those
four cards is addressed by this pull request, and this pull request must not retire any of them.
